comments.body: A data point from 2026-10-25: rad's sprint board (120 cards) was folded into its main board by hand, since kan has no cross-board move. What it took: git mv each card file and set its column; rewrite refs on the moved cards (sprint:X and main:X both became bare X, while bugfixes:X and other projects' refs stayed prefixed); rewrite sprint:X to bare X on main's own cards and to main:X on bugfixes cards; edit two other projects (go-snap, nook), whose cards linked sprint:X and whose linked_boards table named the sprint board; copy the sprint's custom fields and options into main's config so no card lost data; then order each column with kan move --bottom, because the moved cards' position keys meant nothing in their new columns. kan doctor confirmed no dangling links afterward. A kan board merge <from> <into> doing the in-project part, plus a printed list of outside projects still pointing at the old board, would have covered all of it except the outside edits. rad commit 3476f00e has the result.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A card's identity is `boardID:cardID`, so moving its file to another board breaks every link to it and turns its own bare refs into refs on the new board. Restoring a deleted card to a different board has the same effect.

See `docs/design/work-across-boards.md`, section "Deferred". Open: redirects left on the old board versus explicit repair, given that kan doesn't write to other projects' boards.
title: Design: moving cards between boards without breaking links
